findings.title: voterKey() is hidden, but leaves the same tag every time
findings.detail: `voters` insert receives persistentHash(… voterKey() …). It cannot be reversed, but the same input always gives the same value, so every call that publishes it can be linked to the same holder. It has a domain separator but no contract address, so if the user keeps the same secret for other deployments of this contract, those publish the same tag. The same tag appears in `register`, `vote`, so those transactions can be tied to one person.
findings.fix: Fine for nullifiers and one-time registrations. Hash a domain separator and the contract's address with the secret (persistentHash([pad(32, "app:tag"), kernel.self().bytes, sk])), and for repeated actions a per-action counter or a fresh random value.

findings.title: choice() is hidden behind a persistentHash anyone can reverse
findings.detail: `ballots` receives persistentHash(… choice() …), but the only unknown input is choice() (Uint<8>), about 2 bits. Anyone reading the chain can try every value (at most 4 tries) and recover it.
findings.fix: Use persistentCommit(value, salt) with a fresh 32-byte random salt kept in private state, or mix a 32-byte secret into the hash.

patch.text: store a commitment with a fresh nonce instead of the guessable persistentHash
notes: Off-chain: implement the `ballotsNonce` witness to return 32 fresh random bytes on every call and keep them in private state with the value; they are needed to open or prove the commitment later.
Anything that recomputed the old value to look this entry up (off-chain code, or a helper such as an exported hash circuit) must use persistentCommit with the stored nonce instead.

findings.title: whether `qualified` is touched depends on amount()
findings.detail: This insert on `qualified` only happens on one side of a condition involving amount(). The public transcript shows which side ran, so observers learn the condition's outcome.
findings.fix: Touch `qualified` on both paths (write the same shape of data either way), or move the decision into an assert.

patch.text: require the condition with assert, so every accepted call touches the same fields
notes: This changes behaviour: calls where `a >= reserve` is false are now rejected instead of taking the other path. If both outcomes must be accepted, the branch cannot be hidden by a rewrite; record a commitment to the outcome instead.
`belowReserve` is no longer written here and can be removed if nothing else uses it.

findings.title: every `post` stores the same tag derived from memberKey()
findings.detail: `authors` insert stores persistentHash(… memberKey() …) as data on each call. The value is the same every time for the same holder, so all of one holder's `post` actions line up, and identifying one identifies all of them.
findings.fix: Store a one-time tag instead: hash the secret together with a per-action public value (a post number, a counter) or a fresh random value.

patch.text: store a one-time tag, hash(domain, secret, entry key), instead of the same tag on every entry
notes: Each entry now carries persistentHash(["contract:authors", memberKey(), key]): different for every entry, and only the holder of the secret can recompute it to prove authorship.

`members.member` still receives the same tag in every `post` transcript, so the transactions themselves stay linkable. To make them unlinkable too, prove membership with a Merkle path that never names the leaf (see zoo/contracts/board-fixed.compact).

findings.title: who receives this shielded coin can be confirmed: its nonce is public
findings.detail: The coin commitment in this transaction is a hash of the coin's nonce, color, value and recipient. The nonce comes from public data only (ledger state, a counter or a constant), so anyone can recompute it. Then ownPublicKey().bytes, the recipient, can be tested against known wallet keys, one hash per candidate. The shielded output hides less than it appears to.
findings.fix: For a mint, derive the nonce from a private seed: evolveNonce(index, seed()) with a 32-byte random seed kept in private state, as Midnight's shielded token tutorial does. For a coin paid out of contract state, sendShielded derives the new nonce from the stored coin's nonce, which is public; do not count on such a payment to hide its recipient.

findings.title: which member made each `claim` call shows on chain
findings.detail: `claim` looks up persistentHash(… memberKey() …) in `members`, and the key of a lookup is part of the public transcript. The tag is the same on every call and equals the caller's registered entry, so each call is tied to that member, and all of one member's calls line up. Proving membership this way is not anonymous.
findings.fix: For an anonymous check, prove membership in a MerkleTree with checkRoot (the path stays private) and spend a one-time nullifier per action; if identifying the member is the design, declare it in tell.json ("circuits": {"claim": {"caller": "identified"}}).

findings.title: the private key of this public key is on the ledger
findings.detail: `accounts` insert receives ecMulGenerator(k), a public key whose private key is k. Here k is computed only from a value this contract also publishes (a hash of seed()), with nothing secret mixed in, so anyone who reads the ledger can compute k: decrypt what is encrypted to this key, or sign as it.
findings.fix: Derive the private key from the secret under its own domain separator, e.g. persistentHash([pad(32, "app:enc"), seed()]), so it differs from every value the contract publishes.

findings.fix: Derive the private key from the secret under its own domain separator, e.g. persistentHash([pad(32, "app:enc"), seed()]), so it differs from every value the contract publishes.

findings.title: voterKey() is hidden, but leaves the same tag every time
findings.detail: `ballots` member receives persistentHash(… voterKey() …). It cannot be reversed, but the same input always gives the same value, so every call that publishes it can be linked to the same holder. It has a domain separator but no contract address, so if the user keeps the same secret for other deployments of this contract, those publish the same tag.
findings.fix: Fine for nullifiers and one-time registrations. Hash a domain separator and the contract's address with the secret (persistentHash([pad(32, "app:tag"), kernel.self().bytes, sk])), and for repeated actions a per-action counter or a fresh random value.

findings.title: choice() is hidden behind a persistentHash anyone can reverse
findings.detail: `event` receives persistentHash(… choice() …), but the only unknown input is choice() (Uint<8>), about 2 bits. Anyone reading the chain can try every value (at most 4 tries) and recover it.
findings.fix: Use persistentCommit(value, salt) with a fresh 32-byte random salt kept in private state, or mix a 32-byte secret into the hash.
